Updated model runs and official DWD briefings expected later today remain the key near-term catalysts.

**Recent forecast updates from the Met Office point to a maximum temperature of 22–23 °C in London on 6 August 2026, aligning closely with the market’s leading outcomes.** After a notably warm Tuesday (4 August) that reached 28–29 °C under sunny, high-pressure conditions, a shift to cooler Atlantic air and increased cloud cover is expected to moderate temperatures. Climatologically, early-August London highs average near 23 °C, so the current setup represents near-normal conditions following the recent heat. Key variables still in play include exact cloud timing and any localized urban heat-island effects, but ensemble guidance keeps the probability mass concentrated between 22 °C and 24 °C. Traders are therefore pricing the highest likelihood around the central forecast values, with rapidly diminishing odds outside that narrow band as resolution approaches.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and ensemble model runs indicate a moderating westerly flow and high pressure building across southern England, producing mostly dry conditions with sunny spells for London on August 7. After midweek cooling that capped peaks near 22 °C, daytime maximums are expected to recover into the mid-20s as insolation increases surface heating without strong advection of warmer air masses. This positions the 25–26 °C outcomes as the narrowest cluster in trader pricing, reflecting tight model consensus around those thresholds and the low probability of either a sharp frontal intrusion or prolonged clear-sky amplification pushing values higher. Updated short-range guidance over the next 48 hours will refine whether subtle ridge strengthening can add an extra degree.

With historical early-August normals near 23–25°C, the current market clustering near 27°C captures the consensus on a modestly above-average day driven by residual warm advection ahead of the front. Updated model runs and morning soundings over the next 48 hours are the key data releases likely to narrow the probabilities further.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts from the Met Office and other models point to a peak temperature of 25–26°C in London on August 7, 2026, under building high pressure that favors sunny intervals and a warming trend after recent cooler conditions.** 

This setup explains the tight market split, with 25°C at 34.5% and 26°C at 31.5% reflecting genuine uncertainty in model runs about the exact maximum. Key variables include the strength and position of the high-pressure ridge, which determines how much warm air advects from the continent, potential afternoon cloud development that could cap heating, and London’s urban heat-island effect that often adds 1–2°C to official readings. 

Ensemble guidance shows limited spread for the date, but small shifts in timing or boundary-layer mixing could easily push the daily high one degree either way. Updated model runs and official Met Office briefings over the next 48 hours will likely tighten probabilities around the observed maximum, as resolution hinges on the verified peak from approved stations.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Tokyo’s August 6 high temperature centers on 31–33 °C outcomes, reflecting the Japan Meteorological Agency’s (JMA) forecast of above-normal August temperatures and the typical early-August climatology for the Tokyo metropolitan area.**

After the rainy season ended across much of eastern Japan in late July, a strengthened Pacific high has maintained warm, stable conditions with limited cloud cover and southerly flow, supporting daytime highs in the low-to-mid 30s. Recent observations reinforce this: Tokyo recorded 29 °C on August 4—slightly below the early-August average of roughly 30–31 °C—yet JMA’s seasonal outlook explicitly calls for continued above-normal heat through mid-August. Ensemble guidance and historical analogs for post-Baiu periods show the 31–33 °C range occurring on the majority of early-August days under similar large-scale patterns, while probabilities drop sharply outside 30–34 °C because sustained ridging rarely allows either cooler maritime intrusions or extreme heat spikes this early in the month. The market’s heavy weighting toward 32 °C (44.5 %) therefore captures both the current model consensus and the narrow historical distribution around Tokyo’s official observation site.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecast models from the Japan Meteorological Agency show a maximum temperature near 32°C for Tokyo on August 6, consistent with the market-implied leader at 48.5%. This outcome stems from a dominant subtropical high-pressure ridge promoting light winds, moderate humidity, and limited cloud cover that allows typical summer insolation without excessive heating. Historical August baselines in central Tokyo average 31–33°C, influenced by the urban heat island effect and occasional sea breezes from Tokyo Bay. Recent upper-air observations indicate stable steering patterns with no nearby typhoons or fronts expected to disrupt conditions, though model ensembles retain some spread due to small-scale convective variability. Updated runs tomorrow will refine guidance ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance forecasts a 33°C maximum in Tokyo on August 7 under mostly cloudy skies, driven by moderate Pacific high pressure and limited afternoon solar heating. This aligns with seasonal climatology showing typical early-August maxima near 31–32°C in the humid subtropical regime, while the broader 2026 summer outlook anticipates above-normal temperatures from an extended Pacific high. Updated model consensus supports this narrow band without strong upward revisions, though variable cloud timing and steering patterns introduce uncertainty around intensification to 34°C or cooling to 32°C. Real-time observations and next model runs will refine the resolution criteria based on the official daily high.
